behavioral-learning-confirms-contingenci: Shock expectancy ranked the cues by their current danger in every phase, and followed the cues through the reversal.
context-specificity-increases-reversal: Patterns for the two contexts grew more distinct during reversal than during acquisition, most clearly in prefrontal cortex.
context-specificity-predicts-acquisition: Sharper prefrontal context coding revives the once-dangerous cue's acquisition pattern in ACC, the once-safe cue's in precuneus.
context-specificity-predicts-reinstateme: Even in wholly new contexts, sharper prefrontal context coding predicts reviving the newly dangerous cue in middle temporal gyrus.
context-specificity-predicts-reversal-re: In the old context, sharper prefrontal context coding predicts dmPFC reviving the newly dangerous cue's reversal pattern.
cs-plus-univariate-fear-network-acquisit: During acquisition, threatening cues drive more activity than safe cues in dACC, superior frontal gyrus and caudate nucleus.
cue-generalization-increases-acquisition: During fear acquisition, different threatening cues come to share one pattern in the fear network instead of staying distinct.
cue-generalization-limited-dacc-reversal: After reversal, the shared pattern for consistently threatening cues survives only in dACC, not across the wider fear network.
current-threat-activates-fear-network-re: After reversal, currently dangerous cues drive more fear-network activity than currently safe ones, whatever they meant before.
dmpfc-reinstates-acquisition-traces-gene: Back in the original context, dmPFC revives category-level patterns from acquisition rather than from the new-context test.
dual-strategy-reversal-generalize-plus-s: Reversal learning lumps the currently dangerous cues together while keeping the cue whose threat value changed separate.
generalized-pattern-cs-minus-plus-revers: After reversal, the newly dangerous cue takes on the same shared fear-network pattern the originally feared cue had.
hypothesis-context-specificity-supports-: Prefrontal cortex codes contexts as distinct patterns, and that distinctness lets an old fear memory return in its own context.
hypothesis-dual-strategy-reversal: The fear network lumps currently dangerous cues together while higher-order cortex keeps the cues whose meaning changed apart.
hypothesis-fear-network-generalizes-thre: The fear network codes dangerous cues as a class, so any cue that becomes dangerous inherits the class representation.
ifg-reinstates-reversal-traces-item-spec: Inferior frontal gyrus revives cue-specific patterns from the most recent learning, the reversal phase, rather than earlier ones.
item-stability-persists-test-phases: Individual cues keep their own stable patterns in temporal cortex through the shock-free tests, while class patterns do not.
item-stability-precuneus-pfc-reversal: During reversal, precuneus and prefrontal cortex hold a distinct, stable pattern for the cue whose threat value changed.
lss-unreinforced-trials-only: All pattern-similarity analyses use only trials without a shock, dropping the trials likely to carry the strongest fear responses.
no-bold-differences-test-phases: In the two test phases no cue drove more overall activity than another, though participants still expected shocks differently.
no-item-stability-difference-acquisition: During acquisition, a cue's own pattern was no more stable for threatening than for safe cues anywhere in the brain.
pfc-context-specificity-predicts-renewal: Participants whose prefrontal cortex coded contexts more distinctly during reversal showed more fear renewal at test.
prediction-context-specificity-increases: Prefrontal context patterns should grow more distinct during reversal than acquisition, when context begins to predict danger.
prediction-cs-minus-plus-generalizes-rev: During reversal the newly dangerous cue should take on the same shared fear-network pattern the originally feared cue acquired.
prediction-cue-generalization-fear-netwo: Threatening cues should share patterns more than safe cues do, in dACC, superior frontal gyrus, caudate and insula.
prediction-item-stability-changing-cues-: Cues whose threat value changed should hold more stable individual patterns in precuneus, IFG and prefrontal cortex.
prediction-pfc-context-specificity-track: Participants whose prefrontal cortex codes contexts more distinctly should revive acquisition fear memories more strongly at test.
prior-threat-activates-fear-network-weak: Cues that were dangerous before but are safe now still stir the fear network weakly, a trace of the original fear memory.
rsa-roi-derived-from-searchlight: The regions tested in the follow-up analyses were picked from significant clusters in the same data, which inflates significance.
trace-conditioning-hippocampus-engaged: The study uses trace conditioning, a gap between cue and shock, assuming from prior work that this engages the hippocampus.
